# Baseline: reproducing the published TaH+ 1.7B results

<!-- Generated by analyze.py; edit README.template.md. -->

## Summary

We re-ran the published evaluation of the TaH+ 1.7B checkpoint on nine benchmarks with the engine from [chapter 1](../1-engine/README.md), with three random seeds (42, 1234, 2024), following the pre-registered protocol R2 ([protocol](../PROTOCOL.md)). With the code prompt the paper's setting calls for, **{{n_reproduced}} of 9 benchmarks reproduce the paper** (its value lies inside our 95% confidence interval); the exception is {{gap_list}}. The 9-benchmark average is {{avg_tah2}}% (95% CI {{avg_tah2_ci}}) against the paper's {{avg_paper}}%: {{avg_tah2_status}}. The code prompt matters: that of the harness we started from gives MBPP+ only {{mbpp_harness}}% against the paper's {{mbpp_paper}}%, because the model writes code without reasoning and, in about half of the failed tasks, names the function differently from the tests; the authors' later prompt, which lets the model reason first, gives {{mbpp_tah2}}%.

## What was done

- **Setup.** Checkpoint `nics-efc/TaH-plus-1.7B`, temperature 0.6, top-p 0.95, top-k 20, decider threshold 0.9 (the level above which the model's decider sends a token through a second pass). Answers use up to 8192 new tokens (4096 for GSM8K and MMLU-STEM), as in the paper, and are **chain-of-thought**: the model writes out its reasoning before the final answer. A seed fixes the random choices of sampling; each seed is one complete run of all nine benchmarks.
- **pass@1** is the share of sampled answers that are right: the chance that a single attempt solves the problem. AIME25 and AMC23 have few problems, so 8 answers are drawn per problem there and 1 elsewhere. A HumanEval+ or MBPP+ answer is right only if its code passes the original and the extra EvalPlus ("+") tests; an answer with no usable code counts as a failure, as in EvalPlus.
- **Statistics.** Each problem's answers are averaged over the three seeds ({{answers_multi}} answers per problem for AIME25/AMC23, {{answers_single}} elsewhere); the score is the mean over problems. The **standard error (SE)** is the spread of the problem averages divided by √(number of problems): how much the score would move with other problems of the same kind. The **95% confidence interval (CI)** is the score ± {{z}} SE, a range that covers the true accuracy in 95% of repetitions. A benchmark is **reproduced** if the paper's value lies inside our CI; otherwise we report the **gap** (ours minus paper). The paper's single run has noise of its own (binomial SE about {{paper_se_range}} points for the one-sample benchmarks). The 9-benchmark average is the unweighted mean of the nine scores, as in the paper.
- **Two code prompts.** The registered runs used the harness's code prompt. After seed 42 we amended the protocol: HumanEval+ and MBPP+ were rerun with the authors' later code prompt (the "TaH2 prompt"), which the paper comparison uses; harness-prompt results are shown for comparison. Why: [below](#code-benchmarks-why-the-code-prompt-changed).

### Code benchmarks: why the code prompt changed

The paper states pass@1 "under a zero-shot CoT setting" (zero-shot: no worked examples in the prompt; CoT: chain-of-thought) and gives no code prompt. The harness we started from (the authors' first public evaluation code) appends the start of the answer itself, "Below is a Python script with a self-contained function that solves the problem and passes corresponding tests:" and an opened code block, so the model writes code at once, with **no chain-of-thought**, which does not match the stated setting. The authors' later harness (October 2026) lets the model reason first; its MBPP prompt lists the test cases and requires that "the function name and signature must match exactly as specified in the test cases". We adopted it as the TaH2 prompt.

Each failed task is put into one category, from the graded code and the name of the function the tests call (the **entry point**). Harness-prompt answers are first cleaned by EvalPlus **sanitize** (keeps the entry point, the code it uses and the imports); TaH2-prompt answers go through block extraction (first Python code block that defines a function, else the last block). Categories: **wrong logic** (entry point defined, a test fails), **entry point not defined** (functions defined, none under the tested name) and **no usable code**, mostly **empty at cap**: the answer hit the {{cap}}-token limit while still reasoning, so no code was extracted. Per-seed table and examples: [appendix](APPENDIX.md).

With the harness prompt MBPP+ is far below the paper, even below its score for the plain Qwen3-1.7B model without TaH. The model names the function differently from the tests in {{naming_h_range}} of the {{failures_h_range}} failed MBPP+ tasks per seed, although the prompt contains an example test with the right name; in seed 42 these are {{h42_naming}} of the {{h42_base}} tasks that fail even the original tests ({{h42_naming_base_share}}%). HumanEval+ is unaffected: its prompt starts with the function signature. With the TaH2 prompt, naming failures drop to {{naming_t_range}} per seed, and {{rescued}} of the {{naming_h_total}} harness-prompt naming failures (all seeds) pass in the same seed. The cost: answers that reason until the {{cap}}-token limit and produce no code (MBPP+ {{capped_mbpp}}, HumanEval+ {{capped_he}} per seed 42 / 1234 / 2024; harness prompt: {{capped_harness}} in all runs).

## Limitations and negative results

- MBPP+ and HumanEval+ depend strongly on the prompt. The paper gives no code prompt; the TaH2 prompt is our best reconstruction, not a confirmed match.
- With the TaH2 prompt many failures reason past the {{cap}}-token limit without code; a longer limit would change these numbers but not match the paper's setting.
- GPQA-Diamond is not reproduced ({{gap_list}}); the paper's single run has a binomial SE of about {{gpqa_paper_se}} points itself.
- An empty solution is graded as a failure. The TaH2-prompt HumanEval+ grader was fixed before any TaH2 result was graded.
- Missing telemetry: {{incomplete_runs}} (crash-resumed; [appendix](APPENDIX.md)).
